summary: Buildable: scanners, ticketing and config-management tools expose APIs, and a ~15-person R&D team can ship a read-only aggregation, prioritisation and ticketing MVP in 8 months. The risk is scope. Five features, many connectors, cross-tool asset correlation, a curated remediation database and automated fix pushing are too much at once. Push fixes and wide connector coverage should come later.

objections.objection: The MVP is too broad for 8 months: connectors to scanners, code-testing, cloud, CMDB and ticketing, plus prioritisation, a remediation database, an orchestration engine with Puppet/Chef/Ansible push, and validation reporting. Each is a product line. Without cuts, the MVP slips or ships shallow everywhere.

Deduplicating findings across scanners and code tools needs asset identity resolution: matching IPs, hostnames, cloud instance IDs and repos against an often-stale CMDB. Enterprise asset data is messy, so a 'prioritised, deduplicated plan within a day' is optimistic. Correlation errors will undermine trust in the prioritisation.

A remediation database of patches, scripts and workarounds for each vulnerability, across thousands of new CVEs a year and many OS and application versions, is a continuous content-engineering job. It needs a dedicated research team and QA, because a wrong script breaks production. It is not a one-time build.

Pushing fixes through Puppet, Chef or Ansible needs write credentials into configuration management, change-window awareness and rollback. Patches can cause regressions. The MVP should create tickets and generate playbooks for humans to run, with automated push held back until customers ask for it.
Validation depends on scanner rescan cadence, which is often weekly or monthly. That makes closed-loop proof slow and the beta's 2-week time-to-fix measurement noisy.
Every scanner, ticketing system and cloud API change breaks connectors. Integration upkeep will take an increasing share of R&D.

strongest_point: Agentless and API-only, with no own scanning, agents or network taps. This avoids the hardest engineering and runs on data customers already have, which suits a small, strong R&D team.
what_would_change_my_mind: A scoped MVP limited to the top 3 network scanners plus Jira and ServiceNow, with ticket and playbook generation but no automated push.
Asset correlation of 90% or better on 3 design partners' real data within the first day.
A remediation-content pipeline that drafts fixes from vendor advisories and NVD at a measured cost per CVE.
